result.title: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
result.summary: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is critical for autonomous perception, yet its performance is known to degrade in adverse weather. While existing literature models snow as atmospheric noise that degrades performance, our granular evaluation on the WADS-3D and CADC datasets reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: detection accuracy consistently improves as snow intensity increases. Through ablation study and meta-information analysis, we reconcile this by confirming that while falling snow acts as noise, its negative impact is outweighed by a dominant, concurrent factor: significantly increased object point count. We hypothesize that this object point count boost acts as a geometric enhancement, driven by snow accumulation increasing vehicle surface area and a shift from specular to diffuse reflectance. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating perception systems using broad weather-severity bins without accounting for correlated object-level data can lead to misleading conclusions about detector robustness. We conclude that accurate evaluation requires decoupling atmospheric noise from surface accumulation effects and outline future research to validate these physical models. The WADS-3D dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/wads-3d/.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在 WADS-3D 与 CADC 上细致评估 LiDAR 目标检测，发现雪强度上升反而使检测精度提高，并通过消融与元信息分析指出落雪噪声的负面影响被「目标点数显著增加」这一共存因素掩盖，进而主张评估需解耦大气噪声与表面累积效应。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线只有间接联系：其解耦混淆元因素、按细粒度条件评估的思路可供核查，可能启发 latent 推理评价中收益来源的归因（如区分 latent 使用与视觉旁路等共变因素），但领域与任务差异较大，需较多迁移工作。
